summary.intent: Continue a multi-workstream change in the wisp-plugins repo (review-slop-evaluation worktree); this segment covers committing WS2 and implementing WS3, a light fix-pass entry for the `smith` plugin agents (implementer/reviewer).
summary.outcome: WS2 was committed (720add75, 52 tests passing). WS3 edits were applied to the smith agents and related docs, the Codex catalog was updated to declare conventions.md for smith and ranger, Codex output was regenerated, and fix-pass parity was added to the Codex-native smith skill, with checks re-run.

repo: The repo ships plugins (e.g. smith, ranger) with both Claude agent definitions (plugins/smith/agents/*.md) and generated/Codex-native output; changes to one need parity in the Codex skill.
The Codex catalog declares runtime_files per plugin; adding a shared file like conventions.md requires declaring it for each plugin that uses it (smith and ranger).
Plugin changes touch multiple surfaces: manifest, changelog, README rows/anchors, constitution invariants line, and ranger adversary invariants sweep.
Codex output is regenerated by a script and then validated by a set of checks that must be re-run after catalog edits.
workflow: Rewriting JSON via a parser reformats the entire file and creates diff noise; for catalogs, prefer minimal text insertion to preserve formatting.
Writing edit scripts to a temp file (e.g. ws3.py) and applying edits, regenerating outputs and running checks in one step makes iteration fast.
Reading the Codex-native counterpart after editing the primary agents helps catch parity gaps.
